details.label: Summary
details.text: Strong to locally severe storms are possible overnight

details.label: Discussion
details.text: A bowing segment associated with a long-lived MCS is moving northeastward across south-central NE. While this system has generated a well-defined MCV, convection has shown a weakening trend early this morning, with only sporadic severe gusts noted over the last 1-2 hours. Some rejuvenation of convection along the gust front cannot be ruled out as it moves within an elevated buoyancy gradient and zone of low-level warm advection, but the remaining severe-gust threat with this system is currently expected to remain isolated. Farther east, an arc of elevated convection has developed early this morning from northeast NE into southwest IA. This convection has developed within the warm-advection regime to the north of a surface front draped across northern KS/MO. Storms may continue to increase in coverage as they spread northeastward with time overnight. Relatively steep midlevel lapse rates and MUCAPE increasing above 2000 J/kg will favor vigorous updrafts. Mid/upper-level flow is generally weak, and effective shear for storms rooted around 850 mb is less than 30 kt. Given the weak shear, the overnight severe threat is expected to remain rather isolated. However, effective SRH will be more favorable for storms that can become rooted closer to the surface, which could result in at least transient storm organization. Isolated hail will be possible with the strongest cells, while the favorable buoyancy and large PW (near/above 2 inches) will support localized downburst potential, even with the persistence of a near-surface stable layer
